statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 13% (low), Stress 52% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high).
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Elevated attention is flagged for the 19:00-21:00 UTC window, which covers the US cash close at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures settlement at 21:00 UTC. After settlement no live price path exists until the Sunday 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and Monday 7 September is the Labor Day holiday, so the next US cash session is Tuesday 8 September.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes out a two-way session near unchanged; a falling VIX and orderly yields keep Tail low into the pre-holiday futures settlement
body: The Nasdaq-100 is 29,493.31, up 0.04% against a 29,482.32 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered back to mid-range. Retracements have repeatedly occurred in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure this Tail score measures. Volatility confirms the reading: VIX is 14.18, down 0.98% on the day, inside a narrow 13.80-14.36 range. The August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 55,000 expected, with unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% month-on-month to $37.75, moving September Fed hike pricing to around even. Rate transmission has stayed orderly rather than disorderly: the 2-year is 4.39%, up about 3 basis points, the 5-year is 4.550% and the 10-year is 4.784%, up about 2 basis points inside a 4.748-4.812 range. Internals are unusually split rather than aligned, which argues against a single directional impulse: semiconductors are firm, with Micron up 4.24%, AMD up 3.66%, Arm up 3.20% and Intel up 3.18%, while Apple is down 2.17%, Microsoft down 1.80%, Alphabet down 1.19% and Tesla down 6.40%. Single-name damage is concentrated rather than systemic, with Lululemon down roughly 18% on guidance and Fair Isaac down about 16%. Energy remains the principal unresolved background channel, with WTI at $91.44 and Brent at $96.21 held up by continuing US-Iran hostilities and constrained Strait of Hormuz transits. Stress at 52% carries the event weight, the elevated energy complex and the three-day weekend gap exposure; Tail at 13% reflects an observed price path in which mean reversion has been available in both directions all session.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours cover a calm overnight regime, the August payroll release and its decay. Tail drifted between 12% and 17% through the Asian and European sessions while Stress climbed steadily into the print. The 12:00 UTC hour carried the only genuine spike, with Tail at 24%, Stress at 76% and Confidence down to 74% as event/whipsaw mode took over. Price discovery then proved orderly: Tail decayed through 20%, 18%, 17%, 15%, 14% and 13% over the following six hourly assessments as retracements appeared and volatility fell, and the mode reverted to mixed. No hour in the window required a blocking action.
outlookSummary: The last half hour of cash trade is expected to keep two-sided structure with Tail at 13%, easing to 12% for the thin post-close futures hour inside the flagged 19:00-21:00 UTC window. US cash closes at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures settle at 21:00 UTC, after which the entire remainder of this horizon is a halted market with no live price path; forecast Tail therefore falls to a 4-5% closed-venue floor and the published dominant mode of normal denotes a closed venue rather than a resolved regime. Residual Stress in the 36-39% band carries what cannot price until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, principally unresolved US-Iran hostilities with Brent near $96, and secondarily near-even September Fed hike pricing. Monday 7 September is the Labor Day holiday, so the next US cash session is Tuesday 8 September and the next scheduled US macro checkpoints are PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September.
